metadata.title: Divisibility: Learn the Small Test, Not the Big Division
metadata.description: Use divisibility rules for 2,3,4,5,8,9,10,11,15,16,18 and composite divisors, including missing-digit problems.

content.text: Use the smallest relevant part of a number. For 2 and 5, inspect the last digit; for 4, the last two digits; for 8, the last three; for 16, the last four. For 3 and 9, use the digit sum.
For 11, alternate the digit positions and take the difference of the two sums. Composite divisors can often be split into coprime factors, such as 18=2×9 or 15=3×5.
Let's isolate an unknown divisor from a quick arithmetic expression.
When a digit is unknown, turn the divisibility rule into a congruence or digit-sum equation. This is faster and less error-prone than repeated long division.
Now find a missing digit using divisibility by 9.
Nice. Divisibility is now a set of small local checks instead of full-number division.
